# zero-policy

Request rules for zero-server evaluated in Rust: CORS, security headers, Fetch Metadata, request ids, trust proxy, and body limits.

[API reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_policy/index.html) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/zero-policy) | [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-policy)

## The same capability in every language

| Language | Package | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | [`zero-policy`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-policy) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_policy/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-policy), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-policy) |

The TypeScript, Python and C# packages of this capability ship in a later release.

The request rules of zero-server, the rules tier 0 is built from.

CORS, security headers, Fetch Metadata, request ids, trust proxy and body limits,
each an evaluator a handler calls. Rules are data evaluated in Rust, never code
crossing the language boundary. Bearer extraction, rate limiting and timeouts
come in a later release.

`forwarded` holds the trust-proxy rule over `Forwarded` (RFC 7239) and the
`X-Forwarded-*` fields; `cors` the server side of the Fetch Standard's CORS
protocol; `security` the security response headers; `fetch_metadata` the
refusal of cross-site requests that would change state; `request_id` the
identifier each request is logged under; `body_limit` the largest content each
path prefix takes.
